paper.title: Deep Batch Active Learning by Diverse, Uncertain Gradient Lower Bounds

core_method.name: BADGE
core_method.summary: BADGE selects a batch of unlabeled examples by clustering uncertainty-aware gradient embeddings with k-means++ seeding.

paper_claims.method_description: The method forms a gradient embedding for each unlabeled example by combining the predicted class probabilities with the gradient of the final linear classifier. It then uses k-means++ seeding on these embeddings to choose a diverse batch that favors uncertain examples.
paper_claims.claimed_results: The paper reports that BADGE improves active-learning performance over uncertainty-only and diversity-only acquisition methods on image and text classification benchmarks. Its advantage is attributed to selecting batches that are both uncertain and diverse.
paper_claims.benchmark_scale: For the selected SVHN ResNet benchmark, the paper starts with 100 labeled examples and uses batch size 100 through approximately 35,000 queried labels.

try_it_out.definition: Train a classifier on the current labeled set, compute BADGE gradient embeddings for the unlabeled pool, and acquire one diverse batch.

user_provides.name: classifier
user_provides.description: A differentiable classifier returning class logits for a batch of inputs.

user_provides.name: unlabeled_pool
user_provides.description: Unlabeled examples in a tensor or dataset format accepted by the classifier.

data_requirements.format: A finite pool of examples batchable by a PyTorch classifier; classification labels are needed only when training the supplied model.
data_requirements.auto_download_details: MNIST, CIFAR-10, and SVHN can be obtained through torchvision; AG News can be obtained through a standard dataset loader.
data_requirements.synthetic_description: Synthetic vectors with a small linear classifier can demonstrate gradient-embedding construction and batch selection.

dependencies.estimated_time: A smoke-scale selection run should complete in seconds on CPU; model training time depends on the supplied classifier and dataset.

classification.detection_reasoning: The paper is an iterative pool-based active-learning method whose contribution is a batch acquisition rule combining uncertainty and diversity through gradient embeddings; it is more specific than single-point uncertainty acquisition and is not Bayesian MC-dropout acquisition.

comparison.description: The paper compares BADGE with random, uncertainty, and diversity-based acquisition strategies; this package implements only BADGE.

pluggable_component.name: select_batch
pluggable_component.description: Select a diverse uncertain batch using last-layer gradient embeddings and k-means++ seeding.

controlled_variables.unlabeled_pool: Use the same unlabeled pool and preprocessing when comparing acquisition strategies.
controlled_variables.label_budget: Keep the acquired batch size and total labeling budget fixed.

comparison.independent_variable: The acquisition strategy used to select each newly labeled batch.
comparison.evaluation_checkpoints: Evaluate after each acquisition round using the classifier trained on the resulting labeled set.
comparison.primary_metric: Classification accuracy or task-appropriate test error.
comparison.visualization: Plot the selected examples or their two-dimensional embedding projection for a single BADGE run.

model.architecture: A differentiable classifier with a final linear classification layer.

specific_features.why_essential: BADGE scores examples using the gradient of the loss with respect to the final classifier parameters; replacing this with logits alone removes the method's uncertainty-diversity representation.

training.learning_rate: The paper uses benchmark-specific training settings.

data_setup.special_protocol: Start with M=100 labeled examples, then acquire 100 examples for 349 rounds, giving 35,000 total labeled examples; retrain from scratch after each acquisition.

blockers.requirement: Compute per-example final-layer gradient embeddings from classifier probabilities and final-layer features.
blockers.reason: This is the defining acquisition representation and is fully specified by the paper.
blockers.resolution: Implement the final-layer gradient embedding directly from the classifier's final features and class probabilities, then use those vectors for acquisition.

elements.paper_evidence: BADGE constructs an embedding from the gradient of the loss with respect to the final classification layer and uses it for batch acquisition.
elements.required_behavior: Compute one gradient embedding per unlabeled example from predicted probabilities and final-layer features, then use those embeddings for batch selection.
elements.demo_scale_implementation: Compute the embeddings on the smoke-scale unlabeled pool and select the requested batch with k-means++ seeding.
forbidden_substitutions: Do not replace gradient embeddings with entropy, margin, raw probabilities, or input-space features.
Do not replace batch k-means++ seeding with independent pointwise ranking.
required_controls: Use one fixed model snapshot for all candidate embeddings.
Return unique indices from the supplied unlabeled pool and respect batch_size.
fairness_checks: Keep preprocessing and classifier outputs fixed while evaluating the acquisition function.
Do not compare against or implement another acquisition method in the package.
elements.feasibility_rationale: The algorithm is specified in the paper and can run on a small CPU-scale pool.
verification_expectations: The live selector computes final-layer gradient embeddings before k-means++ seeding.
The returned indices are unique and bounded by the pool size.

methodology_contract_pack.summary: The demo must preserve BADGE's uncertainty-aware final-layer gradient embeddings and diverse batch seeding.
implementation_obligations: Compute per-example final-layer gradient embeddings from predicted probabilities and final-layer features.
Select the batch with k-means++ seeding over those embeddings.
forbidden_substitutions: Do not replace gradient embeddings with entropy, margin, raw probabilities, or input-space features.
Do not replace batch k-means++ seeding with independent pointwise ranking.
required_controls: Use one fixed model snapshot for all candidate embeddings.
Return unique indices and respect batch_size.
verification_expectations: The live selector computes gradient embeddings before k-means++ seeding.
The selector returns valid unique pool indices.
